beats.narration: Sailors feared the monster Scylla
beats.caption: Sailors feared the monster Scylla.
beats.action: night storm in a narrow strait: a small ship with one lantern; on the cliff above, long necks uncoil in silhouette
beats.camera_move: slow push up toward the cliff

beats.narration: None knew who made her a lonely girl with a basket of flowers
beats.caption: None knew who made her: / a lonely girl with a basket of flowers.
beats.action: a girl walks alone along a sunset beach, a woven basket of glowing yellow flowers on her arm
beats.purpose: the culprit is a lonely girl

beats.narration: The Greek gods ruled the world and
beats.caption: The Greek gods ruled the world, / and played with mortals like toys.
beats.action: golden halls on clouds above the sea; tall silhouettes of gods at a feast
beats.world_visual: 'The Greek gods ruled the world' → golden halls on the clouds

beats.narration: played with mortals like toys
beats.caption: and played with mortals like toys.
beats.action: a huge golden hand nudges a tiny fishing boat across the sea like a toy
beats.world_visual: 'played with mortals like toys' → a god's hand pushing a tiny boat

beats.narration: Yellow flowers grew where Titan blood had soaked the earth
beats.caption: and played with mortals like toys. / Yellow flowers grew / where Titan blood had soaked the earth.
beats.action: yellow flowers growing out of dark red-black soil, glowing faintly
beats.world_visual: 'Yellow flowers grew where Titan blood soaked the earth' → flowers on red-black soil

beats.narration: Their sap could change a creature into its truest self
beats.caption: Their sap could change / a creature into its truest self.
beats.action: a drop of golden sap falls on a grey sparrow — it shimmers into a gleaming golden bird
beats.world_visual: 'sap could change a creature into its truest self' → a drop turns a grey bird gold

beats.narration: Circe daughter of the sun god was
beats.caption: a creature into its truest self. / Circe, daughter of the sun god, / was mocked by her own family.
beats.action: in her father's blazing hall, Circe stands small and plain among laughing golden relatives
beats.lighting: hard gold, she is in shadow

beats.narration: mocked by her own family
beats.caption: was mocked by her own family.
beats.action: CU: she lowers her eyes; laughter shadows move across her face
beats.lighting: gold flicker on a shadowed face

beats.narration: Then she met Glaucos a poor fisherman who
beats.caption: was mocked by her own family. / Then she met Glaucos, / a poor fisherman who was kind to her.
beats.action: dawn beach: a sunburnt fisherman mends his net; he looks up and smiles at her

beats.narration: was kind to her
beats.caption: a poor fisherman who was kind to her.
beats.action: he offers her a fish from his net; she laughs for the first time

beats.narration: To keep him she fed him the sap
beats.caption: a poor fisherman who was kind to her. / To keep him, she fed him the sap.
beats.action: night: she tips the glowing sap from the flowers into his cup while he sleeps by the fire
beats.purpose: the first use of the flowers

beats.narration: He became a sea god
beats.caption: To keep him, she fed him the sap. / He became a sea god.
beats.action: he rises from the waves transformed: sea-green skin, kelp hair, glowing

beats.narration: A god had no use for Circe
beats.caption: He became a sea god. / A god had no use for Circe.
beats.action: the god looks past her; her outstretched hand drops

beats.narration: He chose Scylla a beautiful nymph
beats.caption: A god had no use for Circe. / He chose Scylla, a beautiful nymph,
beats.action: on a rock in a turquoise cove, Glaucos drapes sea-glass jewels on a beautiful nymph

beats.narration: who flaunted his gifts
beats.caption: He chose Scylla, a beautiful nymph, / who flaunted his gifts.
beats.action: CU: Scylla holds up the necklace toward Circe and laughs

beats.narration: That night
beats.caption: who flaunted his gifts. / That night, Circe poured
beats.action: night: Circe kneels at Scylla's bathing pool, the basket at her side

beats.narration: Circe poured the sap into Scylla's bathing pool
beats.caption: That night, Circe poured / the sap into Scylla's bathing pool,
beats.action: golden sap pours into black water; rings of light spread

beats.narration: to show the world how ugly she was inside
beats.caption: the sap into Scylla's bathing pool, / to show the world how ugly / she was inside.
beats.action: CU: her face lit from below, eyes wet but hard

beats.narration: Scylla screamed
beats.caption: Scylla screamed.
beats.action: morning: Scylla steps into the pool; the water boils gold; she screams

beats.narration: Six necks burst from the water
beats.caption: Six necks burst from the water,
beats.action: six long necks burst up from the water against the sky

beats.narration: six mouths forever hungry
beats.caption: Six necks burst from the water, / six mouths, forever hungry.
beats.action: CU: six fanged heads; in the centre, her own human eyes, terrified

beats.narration: From a cliff above the sea she snatched sailors from passing ships
beats.caption: From a cliff above the sea, / she snatched sailors from passing ships.
beats.action: from a cliff above a strait, a neck strikes down at a passing ship

beats.narration: The gods exiled Circe
beats.caption: she snatched sailors from passing ships. / The gods exiled Circe.
beats.action: exile: a lone island, a small stone house, Circe at the door

beats.narration: Years later she learned how many men Scylla had eaten
beats.caption: Years later, she learned how / many men Scylla had eaten.
beats.action: a winged-sandal silhouette at her door speaks; she freezes

beats.narration: Every one of them was her fault
beats.caption: many men Scylla had eaten. / Every one of them was her fault.
beats.action: she sits on the floor; around her, small lantern ghosts of ships drift and go out

beats.narration: Centuries later she went back to face what she made
beats.caption: Every one of them was her fault. / Centuries later, she went back / to face what she made.
beats.action: an older Circe (grey streak) rows a small boat into the strait

beats.narration: She couldn't undo it
beats.caption: to face what she made. / She couldn't undo it.
beats.action: face to face: six heads loom over Circe; Scylla's human eyes meet hers

beats.narration: So she turned Scylla to stone the only peace left
beats.caption: She couldn't undo it. / So she turned Scylla to stone, / the only peace left.
beats.action: golden light; stone climbs the necks; the human eyes close

beats.narration: Scylla never chose to be a monster Circe did
beats.caption: Scylla never chose to be a monster. / Circe did.
beats.action: dawn: a stone shape on the cliff; birds land on the stone heads; the sea is calm

beats.narration: She wanted the world to see Scylla's true face
beats.caption: She wanted the world / to see Scylla's true face.
beats.action: Circe kneels at a still pool; in it she sees her own face
beats.purpose: OBJECT payoff: the truth about her

beats.narration: In the end the flowers showed her own
beats.caption: In the end, the flowers showed her own.
beats.action: the empty basket on the cliff beside the stone Scylla; one last yellow flower lifts in the wind and falls to the sea. Hold. Fade.
